title: Bytes::copy_from_slice allocates on every put_raw
description: In both ObjectStoreBackend (transit) and ObjectStoreBlockBackend (reader), put_raw does: PutPayload::from(Bytes::copy_from_slice(data)). This copies the incoming &[u8] into a new heap allocation even when the caller already owns the data as a Vec<u8>. put_block takes Vec<u8> by value, so the copy is avoidable there — put_object could accept Bytes directly (or accept Into<Bytes>) and use Bytes::from(data) for the owned-Vec path, which is a zero-copy conversion. For the put_raw path the copy is unavoidable since the input is &[u8], but put_block unnecessarily copies a moved Vec.
